subject: English
passage: A student is writing a research paper on the history of stream-of-consciousness narrative in modern Japanese fiction, situating the publication of Yue Ito's novel Whispered Hours (an influential work of psychological realism released in Tokyo in 1925) within a longer literary tradition. The student claims that some narrative techniques used by twentieth-century Japanese authors of psychological fiction, including Ito, have a lineage that long predates the publication of Whispered Hours.
prompt: Which quotation from a literary historian best supports the student's claim?

choices.A: "The interior monologue passages composed by Heian court diarists in the eleventh century, though brief, employed shifts in temporal perspective and free associative chains that remain central to the techniques used by modern Japanese psychological novelists."
choices.B: "The significance of psychological realism in contemporary Japanese fiction can hardly be overstated, as it shapes much of the prose now taught in university literature departments across the country."
choices.C: "In the decades following the Second World War, experimentation with fragmented narration in Japanese fiction expanded so widely that it became a defining feature of the country's postwar literary identity."
choices.D: "Multivocal narration, a technique developed by avant-garde Japanese writers in the late twentieth century, layers competing inner voices within a single passage. Many works of contemporary psychological fiction now employ this method."

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The student's claim is that some narrative techniques used by twentieth-century Japanese authors of psychological fiction have a lineage that predates the 1925 publication of Whispered Hours. This quotation describes interior monologue passages composed by Heian court diarists in the eleventh century — well before 1925 — and crucially states that these techniques 'remain central to the techniques used by modern Japanese psychological novelists.' This directly supports the claim by establishing both the ancient origins and continuity to modern practice.
